Normal deviates from a private Mersenne Twister

Source: R/likelihood-multiphase.R
dot-hzr_mt_normal.Rd

Reproduces set.seed(seed); rnorm(n) under R's default RNGkind(), bit for bit, without touching .Random.seed. Written out rather than called because calling it means writing to the global environment, and changing the numbers would change which optimum existing multiphase fits reach. The 32-bit words are held in doubles: every product stays below 2^53, so the arithmetic is exact.

Usage

.hzr_mt_normal(seed, n)

Arguments

seed

Single whole number within integer range.

n

Number of deviates.

Value

Numeric vector of length n.

Details

The generator is that of Matsumoto and Nishimura (1998). The seeding, the zero-word substitution and the inversion are derived from R's own src/main/RNG.c and src/nmath/snorm.c, and a test pins them against set.seed() and rnorm(). See system.file("COPYRIGHTS", package = "TemporalHazard").

References

Matsumoto M, Nishimura T (1998). Mersenne Twister: a 623-dimensionally equidistributed uniform pseudo-random number generator. ACM Transactions on Modeling and Computer Simulation, 8(1), 3-30. doi:10.1145/272991.272995
